passages.text: Thus, the power of a monarch does not necessarily make him worthy; nor do poverty and a low station necessarily make a man unworthy. The worthy and the unworthy are differentiated by the worthiness and unworthiness of their acts.
passages.note: Worth comes from actions, not status or wealth

passages.text: Do not swerve from the path of virtue; do not bring about your own good deeds,--lest your labour be lost. Do not make for wealth; do not aim at success,--lest you cast away that which links you to God.
passages.note: Chasing success and wealth costs what matters most

passages.text: "The wise man," answered Complacency, "acts for the common weal, in pursuit of which he does not overstep due limits. Wherefore, if there is a sufficiency, he does not strive for more. He has no use for more, and accordingly does not seek it.
passages.note: Knowing when enough is enough; contentment over striving

passages.text: "Happiness," said Complacency, "is to be found in contentment. Too much is always a curse, most of all in wealth.
passages.note: Happiness in contentment; excess and wealth as burdens
